transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Well, what brings me in is... I just cannot seem to keep my work in order anymore. I work down at the dry cleaners, and lately, my counter is just a complete disaster. I’ve got claim tickets, receipts, workshop notes, and customer jobs all piled together in this huge mountain until I honestly do not know what to handle first. 

Speaking of customers, Mrs. Higgins came in yesterday with this beautiful vintage silk blouse—it had a massive red wine stain right on the collar. I told her, "Mrs. Higgins, you know club soda is a myth, you should have brought it straight to me!" But she insisted on trying to scrub it out herself first at her dinner party, which just ruins the fibers, you know? Silk is so incredibly delicate. My sister actually gave me a lovely silk scarf for my 50th birthday a few years ago, but I’m terrified to wear it because I always end up spilling my morning coffee on myself. I buy the dark roast from that little cafe next door to the shop, the one with the green awning? They make a great cup, but the lids never stay on tight. 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the piles at work. Yeah, the receipts and the tickets. I just... I look at it all and I don't even know where to start anymore.
Did you have similar trouble staying organized or paying attention when you were a child?

Oh, gosh, yes. Even way back in grade school. I remember my teachers were always telling my mother that I was a bright girl, but just completely scattered. I was always talking out of turn, blurting things out in the middle of a lesson. Like in Mrs. Gable's third-grade class—she was this very tall woman who always wore these heavy, clunky turquoise necklaces. I love turquoise, actually. My husband bought me a beautiful turquoise ring when we went to New Mexico for our tenth anniversary. We took a road trip, and it was so incredibly hot there, I honestly don't know how people stand the heat in the desert. We went to this little roadside diner and had the absolute best cherry pie, though, the crust was so flaky... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, being a kid. Yeah, so I was always losing my homework papers, and the teachers constantly had to give me reminders to finish my work because I'd just drift off or start doing something else. It drove my mother crazy.
Before age 12, did you already have these attention and organization problems?

Oh, definitely before I was 12. Like I was just saying about grade school, it was always the exact same story. The teachers would tell my mother I was bright, but just completely scattered. Always losing my papers, and they were constantly having to give me reminders just to finish my work. And the talking out of turn! I was always blurting things out. 

I still do that, honestly. Just last week at the grocery store—the big one on 4th street, they just remodeled the produce section, it's so open and gorgeous now—I saw a woman buying those out-of-season strawberries in the plastic clamshells. You know the ones that look huge but taste like absolutely nothing? I just blurted right out, "Oh honey, don't waste your money, they taste like water!" She looked at me like I was crazy. I felt terrible, but it just popped out of my mouth before I could stop it. I really need to mind my own business. The produce manager there is a sweetheart, though, he always sets aside the good peaches for me in July. Peaches make the absolute best cobbler, especially if you add just a tiny pinch of nutmeg to the crust... 

Wait, did I answer you? You asked about how old I was, right? Yes, definitely way before I turned 12, they were always having to remind me to stay on track.
Do you often feel restless or like you have to move around a lot when you’re supposed to stay still?

Oh, absolutely. I just cannot stay glued to a chair for long. Like, whenever we have those church committee meetings, or even the fabric-care trainings at work, I keep finding reasons to get up. I'll get up for a glass of water, or to grab some papers, or just to check on something in the back. Everybody else is sitting perfectly still, and I'm just up and down, up and down. 

Speaking of the church committee, we're planning the spring bake sale right now, and let me tell you, trying to organize the sign-up sheet is a nightmare. Mildred always insists on bringing her fruitcake, but nobody buys fruitcake in April! I tried to tell her she should make her lemon bars instead, they are just divine. She uses fresh lemon juice, not that bottled stuff. I bought the bottled stuff once when I was making a marinade for chicken, and it just tasted so metallic, you know? I was making chicken piccata, which my husband usually loves, but that time it was just... off. We ended up ordering a pizza instead. We get it from that place on the corner with the brick oven, they do this amazing thin crust with extra mushrooms... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, staying still. Yes, I'm always having to get up and move around when I'm supposed to be sitting.
Did you have any delay in learning to speak as a young child?

No, no, I don't think so. My mother always said I started talking early, actually. She used to joke that once I started, I just never stopped! I was always chattering away about something. 

My sister, though, she was a late talker. We used to worry about her, but she turned out just fine. She actually works as a speech therapist now, isn't that funny? She lives up in Seattle. It rains so much there, I don't know how she handles it. I need the sun. We went to visit her last Thanksgiving, and it poured the entire time. We were supposed to go to this outdoor market she loves, Pike Place, I think it's called? With the guys who throw the fish? I really wanted to see that, but we ended up just staying inside and playing board games. We played Scrabble for hours. I'm terrible at Scrabble, I always end up with all vowels... 

What were we talking about? Oh, right, learning to speak. Yeah, no delays for me, I've always been a talker.
